title: Annotatio IV §.XII close: Irene’s Nicaean iconolaters — bread itself body by conversion — stop before §.XIII
pass_a_gloss: yet on that account about to suffer the heaviest contradiction, under the worst Irene, from the Nicaean Iconolaters, who most sharply contended that the bread in the Sacred Supper is not the Figure of the Body but the body of Christ itself by Conversion — which we indicated more fully in Annotat. 3 §. 3.
pass_b_english: Under worst Irene they met heaviest contradiction from Nicaean Iconolaters, who contend the Supper bread is not the Figure of the Body but Christ’s body itself by Conversion (see Annotat. 3 §.3).
Stop before §.XIII (ninth century; Charlemagne / Bertram reclaiming).
source_text: eo tamen nomine passuri contradictionem gravissimam, sub pessimâ Irene, ab Iconolatris Nicænis, qui panem, in S. Cœna, non Figuram Corporis, sed ipsum corpus Christi, per Conversionem esse, acerrimè contendebant, id quod fusiùs Annotat. 3. §. 3. indicavimus.

lemmas.latin: non Figuram Corporis, sed ipsum corpus
lemmas.gloss: not the Figure of the Body, but the body itself
